task: Critical review of open issues, PR backlog, and governance overhead

events.content: Ran a 3-agent parallel audit (issue taxonomy, PR churn, bureaucracy-cost) against live GitHub state across 92 open issues and 11 open PRs
Closed 9 issues confirmed safe to deprioritize (#5117, #5118, #5115, #5121, #5070, #5043, #4962, #5068, #5014) with evidence-linked comments

Flagged PR #4846 (close_and_restart recommendation) and #4954 (needs_human_call) rather than acting unilaterally on pre-existing owner PRs; handed PR #5036 the exact fix for a 4x-reported unanchored regex

Consolidated the generated-artifacts.md / canonical-source-mirror.md duplicated anti-pattern paragraph into a pointer, regenerated both instruction mirrors, verified push-lock and scoped markdown-lint pass
Hit a live gate defect while pushing: retrospective-policy's {push_files} lefthook template resolves empty on this branch's first push, defeating its own documentation-only bypass

Hit a second live gate defect while honestly completing this session's own sessionEnd checklist: serenaActivated/serenaInstructions are unconditional MUST items with no accommodation for Serena MCP being unavailable, despite AGENTS.md documenting a .serena/memories/ file fallback for exactly this case

The check_sessions() fix unblocked the commit-time hook but not the push-time gate (scripts/validation/checks_tooling.py's validate_session_end): it classifies a session log as new-for-the-whole-branch via a base-ref diff, not per-commit, so a branch-new log is held to full compliance for the branch's entire life. Re-read _validate_required_item_level fully this time (not just validate_must_item) and found it already documents the correct mechanism: demote level from MUST to SHOULD with evidence, explicitly for a harness that genuinely lacks a capability the protocol assumes ('Serena is not reachable from Copilot CLI, and 61 logs say so')

Attempted the SESSION-PROTOCOL.md tier-hierarchy trim previously deferred to 'its own careful pass'. Verified no code enforces the 223-line Tier-Based Coordination section and no incident was cited for it, deleted it, replaced it with a pointer to its cited source (ADR-009). This tripped adr-review-policy (SESSION-PROTOCOL.md is explicitly globbed as governance content requiring adr-review evidence), which is a correct gate, not a bug: this really is the kind of change that rule exists for. Got an independent review from the critic agent before forcing the gate rather than routing around it

PR #5127's Copilot review left 7 comments and its 'Validate PR' check failed a third time on real findings, not process noise: startingCommit in this log named a commit (12051c261) that this session itself produced (so it could not be the session's starting point); the QA report's mypy line examined 0 of 1 files (a scoped wrapper subcommand reported a no-diff-from-origin/main short-circuit, not a real mypy run) so it supported no verdict; the retrospective's session-log inventory (62 + 1436 = 1498) did not match its own stated total of 1492; the retrospective never classified against FAILURE-MODES.md per retros.md MUST-2; three follow-up items in the retrospective had no linked issue per retros.md MUST-4; generated-artifacts.md's fix for the earlier duplication pointed at a `.claude/rules/` path that dangles in the shipped Copilot plugin tree, which ships the sibling `.instructions.md` mirror under a different path, not the source path; and a test class docstring claimed an already-committed session-log edit runs 'the full pre-commit validation', which is now false since --existing-log skips protocol-compliance, evidence-agreement, and QA-evidence checks (confirmed by reading validate_session_json.py:1170-1188 directly rather than trusting the old docstring)

Implemented and shipped issue #5129 as PR #5140 (docs-only QA skip scope verification). CI surfaced two real, unrelated problems along the way: a subprocess-encoding count ratchet regression (fixed by pairing errors="replace" with the new encoding= argument) and a pre-existing main-branch regression, test_every_pr_head_aggregator_is_guarded failing on origin/main itself (5 examined vs a pinned floor of 7) because #5132/#5135 legitimately deleted two whole workflow files the floor was counting. Root-caused via git show comparisons against origin/main at two points in history rather than assuming it was caused by this PR's diff; filed as issue #5142, fixed, and merged separately as PR #5143 since it blocked every branch's push, not just this one
